intro.title: Remove Nth Node from End
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list. You will learn the two-pointer technique, a core algorithm pattern for efficiently solving linked list problems. The main constructs involved are linked list node objects, pointer manipulation, and basic JavaScript loops. By the end, you will understand how to traverse a list once to find and remove a target node.
intro.usecase: The 'remove nth node from end' pattern appears in UI components where users can delete items from ordered lists or sequences. For example, in a task management dashboard, users might remove the second-to-last completed task from a history panel without recalculating positions from the beginning. This algorithm efficiently handles deletion in navigation menus, playlist editors, or log viewers where direct access to the target position isn't available. Developers implement this when building interactive lists that require precise removal operations based on relative position rather than absolute indexes.
